memory_candidates.content: index-entries.json's 'domain' field is a CLOSED enum (core/project/system), enforced by check-extension-docs.sh Rule T. For an extension whose existing entries all use domain="project" (e.g. a domain-knowledge tier like project/logic, project/math), adding a NEW top-level context tier that is a cross-cutting pattern/mechanism rather than domain knowledge should NOT reuse domain="project" -- use domain="core" with subdomain="patterns" instead, following the only existing precedent (the core extension's own patterns/* entries use exactly this pairing). Rule T does not flag an unlisted 'category' field as forbidden, so an extension's existing per-entry 'category' convention can be kept for consistency even though it is not part of the documented schema.

deploy-headless.sh's internal verify-deploy.sh --skip-slow fast-gate pass includes gate10 (specs/state.json schema validation via validate-state.sh --deep), which carries a hard-coded internal 30s timeout. On a large state.json (500+ tasks) under concurrent session load, a direct standalone 'validate-state.sh --deep' run can legitimately take 33+ seconds and still pass cleanly -- the 30s gate10 wrapper timeout is a load-sensitive flake, not necessarily a content defect. Before treating a gate10 timeout as blocking, re-run validate-state.sh --deep directly (bypassing the wrapper's timeout) to distinguish a genuine schema failure from a timing margin issue.
